subject: Pilot commitment, on-call coverage & true-up terms

From: Evan Torres <evan.torres@patchwork.io>

Cc: Patchwork Systems Procurement <procurement@patchwork.io>
Date: 2026-04-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot commitment, on-call coverage & true-up terms

Hi Olga —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Patchwork is excited about the latency and cost profile you showed. Before we scope an initial 6-month pilot, procurement wanted clarity on three items so we can map budget: 

1) Retainer / credits model: if we do an annual commit vs. a 6-month pilot, what credit multiplier and discount do you apply?
2) On-call coverage: we need 24/7 escalation for production incidents; what does Redwood include in the Premium retainer vs. add-on hourly charges?
3) True-up and usage reconciliation: if we provision committed GPUs or vCPU-equivalents, what is the process for quarterly true-ups and overage pricing?

Can you send a short example (numbers) and a draft MAP we can circulate internally? Attaching our initial procurement checklist.

Thanks,
Evan Torres
VP of Platform Engineering
Patchwork Systems

Subject: Re: Pilot commitment, on-call coverage & true-up terms

Evan —

Great questions. I pulled together a concise example and a draft MAP for Patchwork. Key bullets below; I've attached the MAP and a pricing spreadsheet for clarity. Happy to walk through numbers on a call.

• Commit options: 6-month pilot (no commit) vs. 12-month committed capacity. Typical discounts: 10% off per-token price for 12-month low-commit tier, 18% for medium commit, 25% for enterprise commit. We can do a custom credit multiplier if you prepay (example in spreadsheet).
• Retainer credits: Premium retainer converts to blocks of response credits usable against token/embedding usage + priority SLOs. Unused credits are eligible for a quarterly true-up/rollover up to 20% (see MAP).
• On-call & escalation: Premium retainer includes 24/7 phone escalation, one named on-call engineer, and guaranteed response windows (P1: 1 hour, P2: 4 hours). Rapid-engage rotations beyond the named engineer are add-on hours at $250/hr unless you buy the On-Call SLA Bundle (flat monthly fee in the sheet).
• True-up: Quarterly reconciliation based on committed units vs. actual usage. Overage billed at committed price * 1.15 (volume premium) unless you approve a top-up to the next commit band. We include usage dashboards and exportable reports for reconciliation.

Next steps I suggest: (a) pick a commit band from the spreadsheet, (b) confirm target SLOs and on-call headcount, (c) legal reviews the MAP/term sheet. I can join procurement and engineering calls as needed.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot commitment, on-call coverage & true-up terms

Evan —

Thanks for outlining requirements. I pulled the pricing table into the XLS and added a worked example for Patchwork's estimated 6M token/month profile: 

• Example (median band): Annual commit equivalent to 6 committed GPUs for inference + 200M tokens/month -> 18% discount on per-token generation; $12k/month Premium retainer (covers named on-call + 5 hours/month included response work).
• On-call bundle (optional): $6k/month for true 24/7 rotation (adds two additional engineers to rotation + weekly playbook syncs). If you sign for 12 months we can discount the bundle by 15%.
• True-up cadence: Quarterly. If average monthly usage exceeds committed band for two consecutive quarters we trigger a true-up conversation; top-ups prorated to month.

We can offer a one-time 5% commercial concession for a first-year commit if Patchwork signs within 30 days and agrees to a 12-month invoice schedule. I noted that in the spreadsheet under 'commercial concessions'.

If the procurement team wants, I can convert this into line-item language for the SOW and propose invoice milestones.

-Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director of Commercial Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Olga and Stephanie — that helps. Procurement likes the quarterly true-up flow and the dashboards. A couple follow-ups before we run this internally: 

1) Can we get the one-time 5% concession in writing on your MAP?
2) For the On-call bundle, we need guaranteed backup SLAs if the named engineer is unavailable (e.g., escalation to named backup within 30 minutes). Can Redwood commit to that SLA or is that part of the add-on terms?
3) Procurement asked for a cleaner pricing appendix we can attach to the SOW. Could you produce line-item language + invoice milestones we can hand to legal?

If you can return the MAP with the concession and a sample SOW appendix, we'll route through our finance and legal. Once they sign off, procurement will send a PO and we can do a DocuSign for signatures.

Evan Torres
